newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Relatives shocked by US arrests of "bomb plotters".
newsitem.headline: Relatives shocked by US arrests of "bomb plotters".

text.p: Two Palestinians arrested in New York over an alleged suicide bomb plot went to the United States to live the "American Dream", relatives said on Friday.

They said they could not believe news of the arrest of Gazi Ibrahim Abu Mezer, 23, and Lafi Khalil, 22, by U.S. police who say they foiled a conspiracy to target Americans and Jews and bomb the New York subway system.
"His great dream was to go to America and live there...His ambition was to live happily, that's all," said Khalil's uncle, Suheil Mifleh Khalil. "He went there to look for a job."
The uncle, from the Palestinian-ruled town of Ramallah in the West Bank, said his nephew went to the United States last November via Jordan, where the rest of his family lives in Aqaba, and Mexico.
"It's impossible that his ambitions could have changed in such a short time," he said.
"I don't think Lafi belongs to an Islamic group or another political party," he said, adding that he believed Khalil may have been exploited by others or "framed".
Abu Mezer's brother, Nur, said they had last spoken by telephone a week ago.
"He was thanking the American people who are hospitable, who have freedom. Is it possible that a person who says such things would harm them?" asked Nur, a lawyer in the West Bank town of Hebron.
"He has an American girlfriend. He asked me about marrying her. He wants to bring her to meet the family," he said.

Abu Mezer and Khalil were shot and wounded by police early on Thursday when agents raided a ramshackle Brooklyn apartment where they discovered five pipe bombs. Both were in hospital on Friday recovering from surgery for multiple bullet wounds.
A third man is also being questioned by agents from the Joint Terrorist Task Force of local, state and federal agencies, officials said in New York.

Authorities said there appeared to be no evidence directly linking the arrested men with Wednesday's double suicide bombing of a Jerusalem market which killed 15 people, including the attackers, and wounded 170.
But officials said the suspects intended to target Americans and Jews.

"It looks like they were going to set off a suicide bomb and try to make the point that the United States and Israel are wrong and strike against U.S. and Jewish interests," New York Mayor Rudolph Giuliani said.
Nur Abu Mezer said his brother had left Hebron four years ago and, travelling on an Israeli document, went first to Canada and then to the United States to study.
"My brother was a rational man who never supported violence at all," Nur said. "We don't believe this is true. We think there's a mistake in the name," he added.
Khalil's uncle said he had lived in Cleveland and Los Angeles as well as New York, where he worked in a supermarket.
"He could have been exploited because he had nowhere to live. When he first went to New York he was ill and there was nobody to take care of him," he said.
The charges against Abu Mezer and Khalil include conspiracy to damage and destroy buildings and vehicles with explosives.
